reason: We already run our own MCP server, so identity checks, per-customer caps, approval queues and a kill switch are a quarter of work for my team, and we'd rather own that logic than rent it. I'm not putting a pre-revenue vendor with no SOC 2 inline in front of order execution.
objection: It's another hop in the order path: added latency and a new point of failure from a startup with zero customers and no audit. If their proxy goes down or fails closed at market open, my customers' orders stop and that's on me with the regulator.
would_change_my_mind: A completed SOC 2 Type II plus a reference broker running it inline in production with published latency and uptime numbers, or an out-of-path mode (SDK or async evidence export) so a Gate outage can't block an order.
